description: We are a dynamic and multidisciplinary team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our team brings together diverse academic backgrounds in Computer Engineering (CE), Computer Science (CS), and Electronics & Communications Engineering. We bridge the gap between hardware, software systems, and data-driven solutions to tackle complex space and Earth challenge problems.
summary:
On a Mars mission, help from Earth is a light-speed round trip away – often 20 to 45+ minutes. A fever, low oxygen or a failing CO₂ scrubber can't wait that long. LIFELINE is an autonomous onboard medical officer and living digital twin for crews beyond real-time support.

Every astronaut is mirrored by a 3D holographic twin. Each organ is linked to one of NASA's 17 Human Research Program risks and to 20 physiological signals forecast hourly and daily with honest 80/95% uncertainty bands. Our forecasts are back-tested: 87% of outcomes land inside the 80% band 24 hours ahead, and every constant traces to one of 19 NASA, NOAA and JPL sources.

The Flight Surgeon Console triages every alert into Act or Watch, separates ship problems (cabin air, radiation) from body problems, and – when Earth's answer would arrive after the deadline – explains its reasoning and starts the onboard protocol itself. Mission Control adds nine visualization modes, a spacesuit view that projects life support 48 hours ahead, and a phone view for each astronaut.

LIFELINE turns communication delay from a danger into a decision: the right care, on time, beyond Earth.
details:
What it does
LIFELINE is an autonomous onboard medical officer and living digital twin for astronauts on missions too far from Earth for real-time help. On a Mars mission, a question to Earth and its answer can take 20 to 50 minutes. LIFELINE closes that gap by monitoring, forecasting and acting on board.

How it works

  • Digital twin: each crew member has a 3D holographic twin built from a custom Blender anatomy model. Every organ links to one of NASA’s 17 Human Research Program (HRP) risks.
  • Forecasting: 20 signals are forecast from 24 hours to mission end with 80/95% uncertainty bands. These include core temperature, heart rate, HRV, SpO₂, blood pressure, sleep, cognition, hip bone density, optic nerve, VO₂max and radiation dose. The models combine seasonal profiles, split-conformal intervals and Bayesian trends that use NASA population rates as priors. Every forecast is back-tested and graded on its own record: 87% of outcomes fall inside the 80% band 24 hours ahead.
  • Flight Surgeon Console: triages every alert into Act or Watch and tells a ship problem (cabin CO₂, radiation) apart from a body problem. When Earth’s answer would arrive after the action deadline, the Medical Officer explains its reasoning and starts the onboard protocol.
  • Mission Control: nine visualization modes (holographic, X-ray, MRI, thermal, nervous system, realistic anatomy and more), and a “Show me” button that flies from an alert to the affected organ with its forecast and recommended countermeasure. It also has a spacesuit mode covering 22 EVA life-support systems, with an AI monitor projecting oxygen, CO₂, power and cooling 48 hours ahead.
  • Astronaut view: each crew member’s own phone view, for their forecast, reporting where it hurts, logging measurements, and a reaction test.
  • Other tools: HRP risk matrix, countermeasure what-if, race against Earth, readiness, and live space weather from NASA DONKI.

Benefits and impact
LIFELINE turns communication delay from a hidden danger into an explicit, explained decision. Crews get earlier warnings, clear priorities and a trustworthy second opinion when ground support is out of reach. It’s built for Artemis, Mars transit, the Mars surface and the ISS.

Tools and technology
Web application with a real-time WebGL 3D hologram, a 3D anatomy model built in Blender, statistical forecasting with conformal prediction and backtesting, and data constants from 19 NASA, NOAA and JPL sources (including NASA-STD-3001 limits and NASA DONKI space weather). Deployed on Railway.

Creativity and considerations
We combined a cinematic digital twin with honest uncertainty: no forecast is shown without its error bands and track record. We built it as decision support, not diagnosis. The crew data is synthetic but calibrated to NASA-published rates, and every number links to its source. We designed for clarity under stress, separating ship from body, sorting Act from Watch, and always showing how long until Earth can answer.
